mainTopic: The heights of the heavens, and the strict limits on teaching מעשה מרכבה and ספר יחזקאל
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how הקב״ה is surrounded by both light and darkness, and רב אחא בר יעקב adds one more רקיע above the heads of the חיות. The גמרא says this is the limit of what may be discussed, quoting בן סירא. A ברייתא from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי then shows how a בת קול answered נבוכדנצר's boast that he would climb to heaven, by describing the huge distances up to the כסא הכבוד. The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that מעשה מרכבה is not taught even to one person, and lists who may receive its outlines and who may learn סתרי תורה. Stories follow: רבי אלעזר holds back from learning the מרכבה, and רב יוסף refuses to teach it to the elders of פומבדיתא. A ברייתא about where the מרכבה ends is explained as marking levels of teaching. The amud ends with the story of the youth burned by the חשמל, חנניה בן חזקיה's rescue of ספר יחזקאל, and the question of what חשמל means, which רב יהודה answers on the next amud.

steps.title: Light inside, darkness outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes resolving the contradiction about light and darkness around הקב״ה: light is in the inner chambers, darkness in the outer ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is talking about the inner chambers, and that one is talking about the outer chambers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started earlier. Two פסוקים seemed to contradict each other, one about light and one about darkness, and each is placed in a different area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says light dwells with הקב״ה, and another says He made darkness His hiding place. Both are true, because they describe different areas. Light is in the inner chambers and darkness is in the outer ones.

keyTerms.meaning: this one (points to one of the two sources being compared)

phrases.english: [This one is] in the inner houses;
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer from just before: one פסוק talks about light around הקב״ה, another about darkness.

phrases.english: that one is in the outer houses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a resolution of a contradiction raised just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים about light and darkness seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Light is in the inner chambers and darkness is in the outer chambers, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: One more firmament above the creatures
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says there is another רקיע above the heads of the חיות, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אחא בר יעקב said: There is one more firmament above the heads of the חיות, as it is written: 'And over the heads of the חיה there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the awesome ice.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב adds a new level to the picture of the heavens: one more רקיע, above the heads of the חיות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא counted seven רקיעים. רב אחא בר יעקב proves from יחזקאל's vision that there is another רקיע above the holy חיות. The next step says this is as far as one may speak.

keyTerms.meaning: firmament, a layer of the heavens
the holy creatures in יחזקאל's vision

phrases.english: And Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
There is one more firmament
above the heads of the holy creatures,
as it is written:
"And over the heads of the creature was the likeness of a firmament,
like the color of the awesome ice."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an additional level beyond the seven רקיעים discussed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an eighth רקיע above the heads of the חיות.

steps.title: The limit of what may be discussed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this is as far as one may speak. It quotes ספר בן סירא, which warns against probing hidden matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until here you have permission to speak. From here on you do not have permission to speak, as it is written in the book of בן סירא: 'Do not seek out what is too wondrous for you, and do not investigate what is hidden from you. Reflect on what you have been permitted; you have no business with hidden things.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a line. We may talk about everything up to this upper רקיע, but nothing beyond it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Studying מעשה מרכבה has limits. The upper רקיע marks the boundary. בן סירא's words give the reason: a person should focus on what he is allowed to understand and stay away from secrets that are not meant for him.

keyTerms.meaning: the book of בן סירא, an ancient book of wisdom
something too wondrous or beyond one's reach

steps.whatToRemember: The upper רקיע above the חיות is the limit. Beyond it, one may not speak or investigate.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a clear boundary for how far one may go in discussing the secrets of מעשה מרכבה, which is the topic of this פרק.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן יֵשׁ לְךָ רְשׁוּת לְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: Until here you have permission to speak;
phrases.notes: "Here" means up to the רקיע above the חיות that was just mentioned.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ — אֵין לְךָ רְשׁוּת לְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: from here onward you do not have permission to speak,
for so it is written in the book of Ben Sira:
"What is too wondrous for you, do not seek out,
and what is covered from you, do not investigate.
Reflect on what you have been permitted;
you have no business with hidden things."

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן יֵשׁ לְךָ רְשׁוּת לְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the upper רקיע from step 2 as the boundary of permitted discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not speak about anything beyond the רקיע above the חיות.

steps.title: The Divine Voice answers the wicked king
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. He describes the response a בת קול gave נבוכדנצר when he boasted that he would rise above the clouds and be like the Most High.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: What answer did the בת קול give that wicked man when he said, 'I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High'? A בת קול came out and said to him: Wicked man, son of a wicked man, grandson of נמרוד the wicked, who made the whole world rebel against Him during his reign!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens the בת קול's answer to נבוכדנצר. This step sets up the main argument, which comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוכדנצר claimed he could climb to heaven and be like הקב״ה. The בת קול begins by calling him wicked and linking him to נמרוד, who led the world in rebellion. The actual rebuttal, measuring how far away heaven really is, follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
נמרוד, the wicked king who led a rebellion against הקב״ה

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said:
What answer did the Divine Voice answer
that wicked man, at the time that he said
phrases.notes: "That wicked man" is נבוכדנצר.

phrases.english: "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds;
I will be like the Most High"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:14

phrases.english: A Divine Voice came out and said to him:
Wicked man, son of a wicked man,
grandson of Nimrod the wicked,
phrases.notes: Not literally his grandson. He means someone who follows in נמרוד's ways.

phrases.english: who made the entire world rebel
against Him during his reign —

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא that describes the heavens through the answer to נבוכדנצר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בת קול rebuked נבוכדנצר's boast, beginning by calling him wicked like נמרוד.

steps.title: A short life against an endless distance
steps.stepSummary: The בת קול points out that a person lives only seventy or eighty years. Yet just reaching the first רקיע takes five hundred years, and each רקיע and each gap between them takes five hundred more.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many are the years of a person? Seventy years, as it says: 'The days of our years are seventy years, and if with strength, eighty years.' But isn't the distance from the earth to the first firmament a five-hundred-year walk? And the thickness of each firmament is a five-hundred-year walk, and so too between every firmament and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The בת קול continues. It compares the short length of a human life to the huge distances of the heavens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the core of the rebuttal. A person has at most about eighty years, but even the first step toward heaven takes five hundred years, and there are seven רקיעים with gaps between them. So נבוכדנצר's claim that he could climb to heaven is plainly impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: strength (a person who lives longer than usual)
but is it not so that (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: How many are the years of a person?
Seventy years, as it is stated:
"The days of our years are seventy years,
and if with strength, eighty years."
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:10

phrases.english: But isn't it so that from the earth to the firmament
is a walk of five hundred years,
and the thickness of the firmament
is a walk of five hundred years,
and so too between each and every firmament.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the בת קול's speech with the argument from distance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A human lifetime is far too short to cross even one stage of the heavens.

steps.title: The enormous holy creatures
steps.stepSummary: Above all the רקיעים are the חיות הקודש. Each part of their bodies, from the feet up to the horns, is as large as all the distances described so far.
steps.simpleTranslation: Above them are the holy creatures. The feet of the creatures equal all of those distances. So do their ankles, their shins, their knees, their thighs, their bodies, their necks, their heads, and their horns: each equals all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The בת קול goes even higher, to the חיות הקודש. It describes how unimaginably huge they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each body part of the חיות is as large as everything listed before it. The point is to pile up distance on distance, showing how much farther heaven is than נבוכדנצר could ever imagine.

phrases.english: Above them are the holy creatures.
The feet of the creatures equal all of them,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all the distances counted so far, from the earth up through the רקיעים.

phrases.english: the ankles of the creatures equal all of them,
the shins of the creatures equal all of them,
the knees of the creatures equal all of them,
the thighs of the creatures equal all of them,
the bodies of the creatures equal all of them,
the necks of the creatures equal all of them,
the heads of the creatures equal all of them,
the horns of the creatures equal all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the climb past the רקיעים to the חיות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each part of the חיות is as great as all the distances below it.

steps.title: The Throne, the King, and the boaster's fall
steps.stepSummary: Above the חיות is the כסא הכבוד, and above it dwells the King. The בת קול concludes that נבוכדנצר, who boasted he would rise there, will instead be brought down to the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Above them is the Throne of Glory. The feet of the Throne of Glory equal all of them, and the Throne of Glory itself equals all of them. The King, the living and enduring God, high and exalted, dwells above them. And you said, 'I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High'? 'Yet you shall be brought down to the netherworld, to the depths of the pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The בת קול reaches the very top, the כסא הכבוד and הקב״ה above it. Then it turns back to נבוכדנצר and tells him he will fall to the pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After building up the huge distance step by step, the בת קול places הקב״ה above everything. It then mocks נבוכדנצר's boast by quoting the very next פסוק in ישעיהו. Instead of rising to heaven, he will sink to the lowest depths.

keyTerms.meaning: the farthest depths of the pit

steps.whatToRemember: The בת קול answered נבוכדנצר's boast by showing how far beyond human reach הקב״ה is. The person who tries to rise up in arrogance ends up brought down to the pit.

phrases.english: Above them is the Throne of Glory.
The feet of the Throne of Glory equal all of them,
the Throne of Glory equals all of them,
the King, the living and enduring God,
high and exalted, dwells above them,
and you said:
"I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High"?
"Yet you shall be brought down to the netherworld,
to the depths of the pit."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:15, the very next פסוק after his boast.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ: ״אֶעֱלֶה עַל בָּמֳתֵי עָב אֶדַּמֶּה לְעֶלְיוֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the climb and delivers the final rebuke to נבוכדנצר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הקב״ה is infinitely beyond human reach, and נבוכדנצר's arrogant boast will end with him brought down to the pit.

steps.title: The Chariot may not be taught to one person, but outlines may be given
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that מעשה מרכבה is not taught even to a single student. רבי חייא adds that the main outlines may still be passed on.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the Chariot may not be taught even to one person. רבי חייא taught: but you may give him the chapter headings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next part of the משנה: the rule about the מרכבה. It quotes a ברייתא of רבי חייא that softens the rule a little.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to forbid teaching the מרכבה at all, even to one person. רבי חייא says only the full, detailed teaching is forbidden. A person may be given the headings and left to understand the rest on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: The secret teachings about the Divine Chariot (from יחזקאל's vision)
Chapter headings; the main outlines only

phrases.english: Nor the Chariot to an individual.
Rabbi Chiyya taught:
But we may give him the chapter headings.
phrases.notes: Just the main outline. He has to understand the rest on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בן סירא and נבוכדנצר material of the earlier steps and goes back to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשה מרכבה is not taught in full even to one student, but the outlines may be given to him.

steps.title: Even the outlines are only for a court head and someone with a worried heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא limits who may receive even the outlines: an אב בית דין and anyone whose heart is anxious. A second version says it means only an אב בית דין who also has an anxious heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The headings are only given to the head of the court, and to anyone whose heart worries inside him. Some say: only the head of the court, and only if his heart worries inside him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא narrows רבי חייא's permission. He says not everyone may receive even the outlines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version there are two kinds of people who may be taught: an אב בית דין, and any person who worries about his sins. In the איכא דאמרי version there is only one kind of person: an אב בית דין who also has that worried heart. The second version is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: His heart worries inside him; he is anxious about his sins
There are those who say; a second version of the statement

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions differ by just a couple of words: 'וּלְכׇל מִי' (and to anyone) versus 'וְהוּא' (and he). In the first version, two kinds of people qualify. In the second, it is one person who needs both qualities.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
We do not give over the chapter headings
except to the head of the court,
and to anyone whose heart worries inside him.
phrases.notes: He means someone who is anxious about his sins and wants to do full תשובה.

phrases.english: There are those who say,
and only if his heart worries inside him.
phrases.notes: In this version it is one person: the head of the court, and only if he has this worried heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows who may receive the ראשי פרקים that רבי חייא allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The outlines of the מרכבה go only to an אב בית דין and to someone with an anxious heart; in the second version, only to an אב בית דין who has an anxious heart.

steps.title: Five qualities needed to learn the Torah's secrets
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says סתרי תורה are only given to a person who has five qualities. The five are listed in a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: The Torah's secrets are only given to someone who has five things: 'a captain of fifty, a respected man, an advisor, a wise craftsman, and one who understands whispered things.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רבי אמי, gives another requirement for learning hidden Torah. It is a list of five qualities taken from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This widens the topic from the מרכבה to all סתרי תורה. Instead of naming a position (like אב בית דין), רבי אמי describes the kind of person who qualifies: a leader, respected, wise in counsel and in deep understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: The hidden secrets of the Torah
A captain of fifty; a leader

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
We do not give over the secrets of the Torah

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים:
phrases.english: except to one who has five things in him:
"A captain of fifty, and a respected man,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:3

phrases.english: and an advisor, and a wise craftsman,
and one who understands whispered things."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teacher's requirements for who may learn hidden Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סתרי תורה are given only to someone with the five qualities listed in ישעיהו 3:3.

steps.title: Torah is not given over to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי adds a second rule: דברי תורה are not taught to a גוי. He brings a proof from a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי also said: We do not give over words of Torah to a non-Jew, as it says: 'He did not do so for any nation, and they do not know His laws.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement from the same teacher, רבי אמי. It is about who may be taught Torah at all, and it comes with a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps were about hidden Torah. This rule is about Torah in general. The פסוק says ה׳ gave His laws to ישראל and not to other nations, so they are not passed on to a גוי.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:
We do not give over words of Torah to a non-Jew,
as it says:
"He did not do so for any nation,
phrases.notes: תהלים 147:20

phrases.english: and as for His laws, they do not know them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement from the same teacher, attached because it also deals with who may be taught Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דברי תורה are not taught to a גוי, based on תהלים 147:20.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר feels too young to learn the Chariot from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן offers to teach רבי אלעזר מעשה המרכבה. רבי אלעזר says he is not old enough yet, and by the time he is, רבי יוחנן has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to רבי אלעזר: Come, I will teach you the Chariot. He answered: I am not old enough yet. When he grew old, רבי יוחנן had already passed away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells a story showing how carefully great Sages approached learning the מרכבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with a great teacher ready to teach him, רבי אלעזר held back. He felt this learning needs a more mature, settled mind. The cost of waiting was that he lost the chance to learn it from רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: I have not grown old (enough) yet
He passed away (literally: his soul rested)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to Rabbi Elazar:
Come, I will teach you the Design of the Chariot.
He said to him: I have not grown old enough.
When he grew old —
Rabbi Yochanan had passed away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rules about who may learn to a story showing the Sages' caution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר put off learning the מרכבה until he was older, and lost the chance to learn it from רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר turns down רבי אסי as well
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי offers to teach רבי אלעזר the מרכבה. רבי אלעזר refuses, saying that if he had been worthy, he would have learned it from רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to him: Come, I will teach you the Chariot. He answered: If I were worthy, I would have learned it from רבי יוחנן, your teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: a second offer comes, and רבי אלעזר turns it down too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads what happened as a sign. Since he missed learning it from רבי יוחנן, he decides he must not be worthy of learning it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If I had merited / been worthy

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר took the timing of events as a message about whether he was worthy. That shows how seriously the Sages treated learning the מרכבה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said to him:
Come and I will teach you the Design of the Chariot.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי זְכַאי גְּמִירְתַּהּ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ.
phrases.english: Had I been worthy, I would have learned it from Rabbi Yochanan, your teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and ends the רבי אלעזר story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר refused רבי אסי, because missing the chance with רבי יוחנן showed him he was not worthy.

steps.title: רב יוסף and the elders of פומבדיתא agree to trade learning
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף knew מעשה המרכבה, and the elders of פומבדיתא knew מעשה בראשית. They asked him to teach them the מרכבה, and he asked them to teach him מעשה בראשית first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף studied the Chariot. The elders of פומבדיתא studied the Act of Creation. They said to him: Let the master teach us the Chariot. He said to them: Teach me the Act of Creation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins, setting up a trade between two kinds of hidden learning. This step is the setup; the surprise comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side held a different secret area of Torah. רב יוסף asks to receive first, which makes it look like a fair exchange is about to happen.

keyTerms.meaning: The secret teachings about the Creation
Master (a respectful way to address a Sage)

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף הֲוָה גְּמִיר מַעֲשֵׂה הַמֶּרְכָּבָה.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef was learned in the Design of the Chariot.

phrases.aramaic: סָבֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא הֲווֹ תָּנוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
phrases.english: The elders of Pumbedita would study the Act of Creation.
They said to him:
Let the master teach us the Design of the Chariot.
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the words in round brackets, and the corrected wording is the word in square brackets. Both mean 'let the master teach us.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַגְמְרוּן לִי מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
phrases.english: He said to them: Teach me the Act of Creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף הֲוָה גְּמִיר מַעֲשֵׂה הַמֶּרְכָּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about holding back teaching of the מרכבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף asks the elders to teach him מעשה בראשית before anything else.

steps.title: רב יוסף keeps the Chariot 'under his tongue'
steps.stepSummary: After the elders teach him, רב יוסף still refuses to teach the מרכבה. He quotes שיר השירים: things sweeter than honey and milk must stay under the tongue.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they taught him, they said: Let the master teach us the Chariot! He said to them: We learned about these things, 'Honey and milk are under your tongue.' Things sweeter than honey and milk should stay under your tongue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why he will not teach the מרכבה, even after the elders taught him. The story is not over: the elders answer him in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as a rule: the sweetest, deepest teachings are not to be spoken aloud. Keeping the מרכבה hidden is more important than returning the favor.

keyTerms.meaning: Under your tongue; kept hidden, not spoken

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches how guarded the hidden Torah is. Teachers limit who may learn it, students hold back from learning it, and even a scholar who knows it may keep it 'under his tongue.'

phrases.english: After they taught him,
they said to him:
Let the master teach us the Design of the Chariot!
He said to them:
We learned about them: "Honey and milk are under your tongue,"
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 4:11

phrases.english: things that are sweeter than honey and milk —
should remain under your tongue.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנֵינָא בְּהוּ דְּבַשׁ וְחָלָב תַּחַת לְשׁוֹנֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רב יוסף story with his refusal and the פסוק behind it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Deep secrets of the Torah, like מעשה מרכבה, are 'sweeter than honey and milk' and should stay hidden, not spoken aloud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף refuses to teach the מרכבה, because things 'sweeter than honey and milk' must stay under the tongue.

steps.title: A second verse: hidden things stay under your clothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a different פסוק to show that the world's hidden secrets must be kept covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: we learn it from here: 'Lambs for your clothing.' Things that are the hidden secrets of the world should stay under your clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives another source for the idea רב יוסף just used: deep secrets must not be shared openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף used a פסוק from שיר השירים, 'under your tongue.' רבי אבהו uses a פסוק from משלי instead. He reads כְּבָשִׁים (lambs) as if it were כְּבוּשִׁים, meaning 'hidden things,' and לִלְבוּשֶׁךָ as 'under your clothing.' The idea is the same, but the source is new.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, introducing a different source verse
The hidden secrets of the world

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: from here:
"Lambs for your clothing,"
phrases.notes: משלי 27:26. He reads 'lambs' as 'hidden things.'

phrases.english: things that are the hidden secrets of the world
should be under your clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second פסוק for the rule of secrecy that רב יוסף based on שיר השירים.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that deep secrets of Torah must be kept hidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 27:26, 'כבשים ללבושך', read as 'hidden things under your clothing'

steps.title: The elders already learned it, and רב יוסף says that is the מרכבה itself
steps.stepSummary: The elders tell רב יוסף they already learned up to 'And He said to me, son of man.' He answers that those very verses are מעשה המרכבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: we have already learned those verses up to 'And He said to me, son of man.' He said to them: those are the very essence of מעשה המרכבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The elders push רב יוסף by saying they already know the verses. He replies that what they learned is already the core of the מרכבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elders' reasoning is that if they have learned the verses, he may as well teach them. רב יוסף answers that the verses up to the end of יחזקאל's first chapter are themselves the מרכבה. That means he holds that מעשה המרכבה runs through the whole first chapter. The next step challenges exactly this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of man, the opening of יחזקאל chapter 2
These are the very ones, the essence itself

phrases.english: They said to him:
We have learned them
up to "And He said to me, son of man."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 2:1, right after the vision of the first chapter.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הֵן הֵן מַעֲשֵׂה הַמֶּרְכָּבָה.
phrases.english: He said to them: these are the very Design of the Chariot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב יוסף and the elders after he refused to teach them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף, מעשה המרכבה includes the verses through the end of יחזקאל chapter 1.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the מרכבה ends earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף from a ברייתא that ends מעשה המרכבה at the second 'And I saw' or at 'the חשמל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: up to where does מעשה המרכבה go? רבי says: up to the last 'And I saw.' רבי יצחק says: up to 'the חשמל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב יוסף's view of how far the מרכבה reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף treated everything up to chapter 2 as the מרכבה. The ברייתא gives two opinions, and both end the מרכבה earlier, inside verse 27 of chapter 1. So the ברייתא seems to argue with רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, usually from a ברייתא
A glowing substance in יחזקאל's vision

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not deny that chapter 1 is about the מרכבה. The question is only where the part counted as מעשה המרכבה ends.

phrases.english: They challenged:
Up to where is the Design of the Chariot?
Rabbi says: up to the last "And I saw,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:27, the last time 'And I saw' appears in the chapter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says: up to "the electrum."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's claim that the verses up to chapter 2 are the מרכבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's statement that the verses through the end of chapter 1 are מעשה המרכבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא ends the מרכבה earlier, at 'וארא' or 'החשמל,' not at the end of the chapter.

steps.title: Different levels of teaching for different parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the whole chapter is the מרכבה, but it is taught in levels. There are two versions of where the levels change.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to 'And I saw' we teach it fully. From there on we pass on only chapter headings. Some say: up to 'And I saw' we pass on chapter headings. From there on, if he is wise and understands on his own, yes; if not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא's endpoint marks a change in how much may be taught, not the end of the מרכבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב יוסף and the ברייתא fit together. The whole chapter is מרכבה, but the earlier part is taught more openly and the later part more carefully. In the first version, the early part is taught fully and the later part only in outline. In the second version, the early part gets only outlines, and the later part is taught only to someone who can understand it on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Chapter headings, only the main outlines
Some say, introducing a second version

phrases.english: Up to "And I saw" we teach fully,
from here on we pass on only the outlines.
Some say:
Up to "And I saw" we pass on the outlines,
from here on,
if he is wise and understands on his own
yes; if not, no.
phrases.notes: He means: we teach him only if he can understand it on his own; otherwise we don't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא's endpoint as a change in teaching level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא meant that the מרכבה itself ends at 'וארא' or 'החשמל.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole chapter is מרכבה. The ברייתא only marks where the teaching becomes more limited.
steps.whatToRemember: All of יחזקאל chapter 1 is מעשה המרכבה, but it is taught in stages. The deeper parts are taught only in outline or only to the very wise.

steps.title: Can one expound the חשמל at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how anyone may expound the חשמל, since a youth who did so was burned by fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we really expound the חשמל? But there was a certain youth who expounded the חשמל, and fire came out and burned him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the חשמל may be taught at all, even in limited ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step allowed some teaching of the later part, which includes the חשמל. A story shows that expounding the חשמל can be deadly. That suggests it should never be taught.

phrases.english: And do we expound the electrum?
But there was a certain youth who expounded the electrum,
and fire came out and consumed him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the חשמל, mentioned in the ברייתא, may be taught at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the חשמל may be expounded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A youth who expounded the חשמל was burned, so expounding it seems forbidden and dangerous.

steps.title: The youth was not yet ready
steps.stepSummary: The youth was different, because he was too young for such study.
steps.simpleTranslation: A youth is different, because his time had not yet come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the danger was because of the youth's age, not because the חשמל can never be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was the learner, not the subject. Someone mature and ready may study it. This matches the earlier story where רבי אלעזר said he was not yet old enough.

phrases.english: A youth is different,
for his time had not arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the story of the youth.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story proves that the חשמל may never be expounded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone too young is in danger. A mature, ready learner may study it.

steps.title: חנניה בן חזקיה saved ספר יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה praises חנניה בן חזקיה. Without him, ספר יחזקאל would have been hidden away because it seemed to contradict the Torah. He sat in an upper room and expounded it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: indeed, that man is remembered for good, and his name was חנניה בן חזקיה. Were it not for him, ספר יחזקאל would have been hidden away, because its words contradicted the words of the Torah. What did he do? They brought up to him three hundred barrels of oil, and he sat in an upper room and expounded it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new statement about ספר יחזקאל: one man's hard work kept it from being put away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of יחזקאל continues, but now the issue is the book's laws, not the מרכבה. Its words seemed to clash with the Torah, so it was almost hidden away. חנניה בן חזקיה studied it at length and expounded it until it fit, so it stayed in use.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden away, put out of public use

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains how ספר יחזקאל stayed part of the accepted books even though it seemed to clash with the Torah.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Indeed, that man is remembered for good,
and Chananya ben Chizkiya was his name.
Were it not for him, the book of Yechezkel would have been hidden away,
phrases.notes: 'Hidden away' means put aside and not used publicly.

phrases.english: for its words contradicted the words of the Torah.
What did he do?

phrases.aramaic: הֶעֱלוּ לוֹ שְׁלוֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי שֶׁמֶן,
phrases.english: They brought up to him three hundred barrels of oil,
and he sat in an upper room and expounded it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּרַם זָכוּר אוֹתוֹ הָאִישׁ לַטּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מרכבה in יחזקאל to the book of יחזקאל as a whole.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thanks to חנניה בן חזקיה's study and explanation, ספר יחזקאל was not hidden away.

steps.title: The youth burned by the חשמל and חנניה's defense of ספר יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a youth who understood the חשמל and was burned. The חכמים wanted to hide ספר יחזקאל, but חנניה בן חזקיה said that not everyone is as wise as that boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: There was a story with a youth who was reading ספר יחזקאל in his teacher's house, and he understood the חשמל. Fire came out of the חשמל and burned him. So the חכמים wanted to hide away ספר יחזקאל. חנניה בן חזקיה said to them: If this boy was wise, does that mean everyone is that wise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the full ברייתא behind the youth story from steps 20-21. It also shows another time חנניה בן חזקיה saved ספר יחזקאל from being hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger came from deeply understanding the חשמל, not from simply reading the book. חנניה argues that this boy was a rare case. Most readers will never reach that depth, so the book is not dangerous for the public and does not need to be hidden. This fits step 21's answer that the youth was a special case, and step 22's praise of חנניה for saving the book.

keyTerms.meaning: A mysterious glowing thing in יחזקאל's vision
To hide away, remove from public use

steps.confusionAlert: חנניה is not saying the boy did nothing wrong. He is saying the boy's case is rare, so it is no reason to hide the whole book from everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how ספר יחזקאל stayed part of תנ"ך even though parts of it are dangerous to study too deeply.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident with one youth
who was reading in his teacher's house
in the book of Ezekiel
and he understood the chashmal,
phrases.notes: The word חשמל comes from יחזקאל 1:4 and 1:27. It describes something glowing in the vision.

phrases.english: and fire came out of the chashmal and burned him,
and they wanted to hide away the book of Ezekiel.
Chananya ben Chizkiya said to them:
If this one was wise,
are all people wise?
phrases.notes: He means that this boy was a rare genius. Most people won't understand that deeply, so the book isn't a danger to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full ברייתא behind the youth story and adds another case of חנניה saving ספר יחזקאל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספר יחזקאל was not hidden, because the rare danger of deep study of the חשמל applies only to someone unusually wise.

steps.title: What is the חשמל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word חשמל means, and רב יהודה begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the חשמל? רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the חשמל has come up, the גמרא asks what the word actually means. This is a setup line: רב יהודה's answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a plain question about a word, not a challenge. The חשמל was so powerful that it burned the youth, so the גמרא wants to explain what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer

phrases.english: What is the chashmal?
Rav Yehuda said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the word חשמל from the story and asks what it means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word חשמל in יחזקאל's vision
